subject: Probability forecasts for ten binary macroeconomic indicators at one, five and ten year horizons, from a hidden Markov model over latent economic regimes.

primary_endpoint.name: one-year paired difference in mean Brier skill score against main
primary_endpoint.note: Paired over the same 378 resolved forecast dates from 1994-03, moving-block bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 20260908. About 31.5 independent one-year observations.

changes.title: Adopted: the two-chain model is now the pipeline's default
changes.what_changed: Arm A4 merged, so every command — backtest, forecast-now, submit, the notebooks — runs two chains unless a setting says otherwise. Measured as main's own pipeline against the committed single-chain baseline, which was deliberately not recaptured so the comparison keeps a fixed anchor.

recorded.headline: one year +0.0590, 90% [+0.0275, +0.0877], 98.33% [+0.0147, +0.1019]
recorded.detail: five years +0.0465, ten years +0.1855; 281 of 387 fields moved and five moved categorically — the one-year verdict SHIP BASE RATE to SHIP MODEL, its failing gate calibration to none, ten years dropping robustness, and the run identity ad7fcc1affd0746a to fec79a040f9ca6f9 at 6 to 16 regimes

impact.provenance: forecast baseline compare --paired, run after the merge at 19fe4b0; all five gates pass

notes: It reproduces the arm's figures to the digit, because the arm and the adopted default are the same computation.
The submission still carries the old shipped configuration and its manifest; re-shipping needs the owner's token and is a separate decision.
Three independent judges adjudicated the stress-test dossier: all three said adopt, two classifying the decision FACTUAL and one MECHANICAL.
ADR 0010 records what this does not claim: the mechanism is unestablished, and briefing 05's matched-cell evidence points at granularity rather than timescale separation.

changes.title: Two chains: growth, and inflation with rates
changes.what_changed: Two independent hidden Markov chains replace main's single chain. A growth chain drives growth; a levels chain drives inflation and rates. The joint regime is the pair, sixteen in all, chosen as four by four on a burn-in window ending before the first scored date. The joint transition matrix is the Kronecker product and the fit is exact expectation maximisation, because the likelihood separates by chain.
notes: The only arm whose family-wise interval clears zero and survives its independent look-ahead review.
Two further seeds, fixed before they ran, reproduce it: one-year lower bounds +0.0299 and +0.0296 (diagnostic 0004).
Sixteen regimes on 58 free parameters, against main's six on 89; an unrestricted sixteen-state chain would need 399.
Validated for adoption on 2026-09-16: two defects found by executing rather than reading, both fixed, and every scored number unchanged across three re-runs.

changes.title: All Weather quadrants over levels, four states
changes.what_changed: The four quadrants imposed as the state space: every fit has four states, each started from the centroid of one quadrant, split at each series' expanding median so no threshold is written down. The burn-in sweep still runs and would have chosen six; it now chooses nothing.
changes.status: confirmed, but loses the one structure slot to A4
notes: Its registered prediction was that one-year skill would FALL with fewer states. It rose.
A model has one state space, so the combination rule takes the larger one-year difference, which is A4's.
Its deterministic audit tested main's six states rather than this arm's four (debt D15); its reviewer re-ran the audit forced to four states and it passed.

changes.title: All Weather quadrants over surprises
changes.what_changed: The model reads surprises rather than levels: each month's growth and inflation minus a recursive AR(1) forecast fitted only on earlier months, which is how All Weather's primary sources define the quadrants. State count fixed at four.
notes: Faithful to the source, and no better than main.
Came closer to the harm floor at five years than any other arm without crossing it.

changes.title: Sticky prior on the transition matrix
changes.what_changed: A Dirichlet prior on each row of the transition matrix, pulling toward staying in the current regime, at a strength fixed at registration from published estimates.
notes: Main's fit declares some regime switches effectively impossible, with transition probabilities as small as 1e-184; under the prior the smallest is about 0.0014.
Persistence fell as predicted, but the one-year interval straddles zero at both levels.

changes.title: Fixed 50/50 blend with the historical base rate
changes.what_changed: Pure post-processing with the model unchanged: every forecast becomes half the model's probability and half the climatology's, at every horizon and indicator, with no fitted weight.
changes.status: void: its review found a leak by design
notes: The arm's code does what was registered; the leak is in the registered design. Main's climatology is clean only because main's forecasts never read it.
Blending it in gives two known main-level approximations a path into the forecast: the recession lag (at most 0.00083 on a blended forecast) and revised outcome values back to 1919 (up to 0.0047).
Neither could move a verdict. The pre-registration voids an arm for any such path, not only a large one, and the rule was applied as written.

changes.title: Direct per-horizon regime rates
changes.what_changed: Instead of composing each horizon from one-month rates through the transition matrix, each regime's rate of the h-horizon outcome is estimated directly, from months whose outcome had resolved and been published by the refit date.
notes: Its reviewer rebuilt all 11,730 backtest probabilities from the registered formula with independent date arithmetic; every one matched.
The same review found the recession-lag leak now recorded as debt D14.

changes.title: Control: main, unchanged
changes.what_changed: A worktree cut from main with no change at all, run through the same harness as every arm.
notes: Exact zeros at every horizon. Without this, a harness that quietly reported main's own numbers for every arm would have looked like six successes.

changes.title: The benchmark counted outcomes before they were published
changes.what_changed: Main's climatology benchmark counted each outcome h months after its forecast date, before the observation it rested on had been published: 32 to 400 days early.

impact.provenance: measured by the regression harness; ADR 0009

notes: Found by the look-ahead audit the first time it ran, not by review. The pre-registration had already decided the slate halts until main is clean; it halted.
The leak flattered the benchmark, not the model.

changes.title: The recession series' publication lag is too short after a trough
changes.what_changed: The registry assumes a recession month is known 400 days later. NBER announces turning points, not months: every peak since 1990 came within 400 days (128 to 366), every trough after them (474 to 662). All eight announcement dates were checked at nber.org.

recorded.headline: 8 of 391 scored forecast dates, two recession indicators only
recorded.detail: measured in arm A5 at most 0.0025 on a forecast; in A2, dropping the affected dates moves its one-year difference from +0.0381 to +0.0383

impact.provenance: derived from the registry and NBER announcement dates; two independent reviews

notes: Main and every arm read the same registry, so it cannot favour one side of a paired comparison.
The invariance audit could not see it while it perturbed by the registered lag, and its own record said so. It now applies the same announcement rule, by its own separate implementation.
Fix options were a longer fixed lag of at least 662 days, or availability dated by each NBER announcement. The second was taken; ADR 0011 says why.

changes.title: Recession status is dated by the announcement that settled it
changes.what_changed: A recession month is now published at the later of its constant 400-day lag and the NBER announcement of the turning point opening its phase, from a table of the eight announcements since 1990. The pipeline and the look-ahead audit each apply the rule by their own implementation, so a mistake in one cannot agree with the other.

recorded.headline: one year +0.2744 to +0.2673, 90% [-0.0165, -0.0009]
recorded.detail: five years +0.0002, ten years +0.0049 [+0.0014, +0.0136]; 57 fields moved, every one on the two recession indicators, and no verdict changed. One-year skill FALLS and the interval excludes zero, which is the right sign: some of it was earned on post-trough codings no forecaster could have read.

impact.provenance: forecast baseline compare --paired against baselines/a4-pre-d14, the A4-adopted run captured immediately before this change so A4's effect is not folded in; ADR 0011

notes: The first version of this fix introduced a worse leak than the one it closed: it let the announcement REPLACE the lag, and because the announcement settling a month is usually older than the month, values were dated before they existed -- 1995-01 published 1992-12-22. A panel built in 1994-05 could read 74 future labels. forecast audit-look-ahead caught it at 400 moved rows.
The suite was 509 green while that leak existed, because nothing required a publication date to follow its own label. Three tests now do.
Eighteen forecast dates moved where D14 predicted eight; ADR 0011 accounts for all of them.
configuration_hash is unchanged at fec79a040f9ca6f9: this is a leak fix, not a variant anyone would select, so it adds no RunSettings field. The regression baseline distinguishes the runs.

changes.title: The composition's Markov assumption, tested directly
changes.what_changed: The any-time composition assumes a condition depends on last month's condition and this month's regime and nothing else. That was only ever tested indirectly, as miscalibration. Both orders are now fitted on the same months with the same filtered regime weights and the same shrinkage, and compared by log likelihood with a BIC penalty.

recorded.headline: no indicator prefers second order
recorded.detail: pooled, second order buys 32.1 log-likelihood points for 320 extra parameters, dBIC +2847.5 over 909 months at sixteen regimes; the composition does not understate persistence, which is the failure the debt was watching for

impact.provenance: research/derivations/condition_process_order.py, committed and runnable; in-sample on the final model's filtered probabilities, which is the direct test the debt asked for

notes: The two recession rows are identical because both indicators resolve off recession_indicator and share one monthly condition series.
With sixteen regimes the penalty term is large, so the same conclusion is stated from the unpenalised likelihoods too.

changes.title: Two debts answered by the slate that had already run
changes.what_changed: D1 asked what a Dirichlet prior on the transition matrix would change; arm A1 is exactly that fix. D4 asked for the direct per-horizon path to be implemented and compared; arm A5 is exactly that path. Neither needed new engineering, only reading the measurement against the question.

recorded.headline: D1's mechanism confirmed, its consequence contradicted
recorded.detail: the prior does shorten the horizon (lambda2 0.9777 to 0.9700 at 1994-03), but ten-year skill IMPROVED +0.1905 90% [+0.0899, +0.2320] where the debt predicted it would worsen. D4: the direct path fixes the ten-year compounding, +0.2647 90% [+0.0459, +0.2526], and breaks one year, -0.1017, HARMFUL

impact.provenance: each arm's own paired.json, look-ahead reviews CLEAN; experiment 0002

changes.status: closed D1 and D4; neither adopted
notes: D1's entry should not be quoted as though its argument had been borne out. It predicted regularising would strengthen the paper's conclusion; the measurement points the other way, on 2.25 effective independent observations.
D4's data-efficiency cost is visible as predicted: mean effective sample size for recession-within-ten-years falls 98.1 to 39.9.
D7, D8 and D12 were closed the same day by recorded decision rather than by work, because their fixes are new experiments, not repairs.

changes.title: How much the conditions owe to reading final data
changes.what_changed: Conditions are read from final revised values with publication timing enforced but not vintage. The size of that approximation was argued rather than measured. It is now measured: each refit date's archival vintage against the final file, on every month published by then, over all 33 refit dates.

recorded.headline: 34 condition-months in about 54,000
recorded.detail: USREC differs on 10 of 29,541 published months (0.034%), each one a full flip of the recession condition. UNRATE differs on 467 of 24,584 (1.900%) but crosses a threshold far more rarely: 15 flips above five percent and 9 above seven. A revision only reaches a forecast by crossing a threshold, so the flip count is the exposure, not the revision rate

changes.status: closed D5 by measurement; not implemented, by recorded decision
notes: The scope is narrower than the debt reads: of the six series conditions and outcomes require, two are model inputs that already get archival vintages and two are never revised. Only UNRATE and USREC were ever exposed.
USREC's ten flips are D14's phenomenon -- dating revised as the committee announces -- and ADR 0011 now dates those by announcement.

Not implemented because load_final_series takes no as_of and is called once for the whole backtest rather than per refit, so the fix is an interface change plus thirty-three loads instead of one, to correct 34 condition-months.

A trap recorded with it: payroll employment and core prices are revised, are in the registry, and are read by no indicator. Payrolls move in 72% of months and that number describes nothing this pipeline does.

changes.title: The shrinkage strength, swept instead of assumed
changes.what_changed: conditional_rate_shrinkage_strength was set to 10 at the start and left there; nothing established it was better than 3 or 30. The walk-forward now has a committed sweep at five strengths, each scored with the pre-registered verdict's own statistic over all 33 refits.

recorded.headline: one year: 1 +0.2563, 3 +0.2607, 10 +0.2673, 30 +0.2686, 100 +0.2590
recorded.detail: the curve is flat across its top at the endpoint that counts: 30 beats the shipped 10 by +0.0013, more than an order of magnitude inside the paired interval's half-width of about 0.016, so they are not distinguishable. Five and ten years rise monotonically to +0.1327 and +0.0307, but carry about 5.5 and 2.2 independent observations. The value stays at 10

impact.provenance: research/derivations/shrinkage_strength_sweep.py, 5 strengths x 33 refits x 391 forecast dates

changes.status: closed D3; value unchanged, by evidence
notes: Not changed is the finding. What the debt lacked was evidence, not a different number; moving a hyperparameter to chase the long horizons would be tuning on the sample the result is measured against.

The debt's own cost estimate is wrong as the code stands: it budgeted one rate-estimation pass because the fits are cached, but the strength is in RunSettings and therefore in configuration_hash, which is part of the fit-cache key. Every strength missed the cache and refitted all 33 models -- five full refit sets, about seventy minutes -- though the shrinkage cannot affect a fit.

changes.title: One table for everything the pipeline generated
changes.what_changed: `forecast artifacts` lists every generated file with its size, its age and the command that wrote it, across the artifact store, submission/, baselines/ and artifacts/. The artifact-to-command map is read off the call sites and held against ArtifactNames in both directions by a check.

recorded.headline: 18 named artifacts, all attributed; one deleted as unproducible
recorded.detail: run_manifest was declared and written nowhere and read nowhere, so the command would have listed a file the pipeline cannot produce; it is removed with the condition for re-adding it. Building it also collapsed a byte-identical text-table formatter that existed in two modules

notes: The debt's own description was out of date: artifacts/<date>/ holds one graph view from scripts/graph_view.py, not rendered pages, and no pipeline command writes there.

changes.title: Seven modules import across the layer table, and nothing fails
changes.what_changed: The package docstring declares a layer order and says dependencies point one way only. scripts/layer_check.py reads that table as the specification; seven imports disagree with it, in data, features, evaluation and reporting. All seven pre-date this session.

recorded.headline: not correctness, but the docstring's standing as a specification
recorded.detail: nothing here is a cycle; the suite, the gates and the audit all pass. A reader who takes the layer table literally will be wrong about this package seven times, and layer_check exits 0 whatever it finds, so nothing stops the count rising

changes.status: open; the owner decides which side is the defect
notes: The checker states the choice exactly: either the imports move, which is real surgery in data and features, or the table is rewritten to describe the package as it is.
Whichever way it goes, the check should be made enforceable; today it reports and exits 0.

changes.title: The look-ahead audit chose the state count its own way
changes.what_changed: The audit's from-scratch run picks the number of regimes by calling the burn-in sweep directly, while the backtest decides it one layer up. An arm that fixes the count in that upper layer gets audited with main's count instead of its own.

recorded.headline: one arm affected, A2
recorded.detail: its audit fitted six states and never ran its four-state seeding; its reviewer re-ran the audit forced to four states and it passed, all 2,190 rows identical

impact.provenance: found by the arm's author, verified in the code, confirmed by the independent reviewer

notes: Every other arm's audit fitted the arm's own count: A3 four, A4 sixteen, the rest leave the count alone.
Shape of the fix: one function in the backtest layer decides the count, and both the command line and the audit call it.

changes.title: Two failures that only execution could find
changes.what_changed: With two chains as the default, both notebooks raised on loading the fitted model. Fixing that exposed a second failure behind it: a two-chain run persists only the joint sweep table, and a notebook rebuilt single-chain objects from its columns by hand. A display helper had also been creating the missing columns and printing them blank rather than raising.

recorded.headline: no scored number moved
recorded.detail: three re-runs bit-identical, 0 of 387 comparison fields differing, configuration hash unmoved

impact.provenance: arm re-runs against the pinned pre-refactor outputs

notes: A code review found the first failure; only running the notebooks found the second.
A scoped follow-up review then found the fix itself uncovered, which five new checks close.

changes.title: A run that named a commit whose code never ran whole
changes.what_changed: One arm's code was edited while its run was in progress, so its recorded exit codes named a commit that did not produce them.

recorded.headline: that run was voided and re-run
recorded.detail: the re-run on a clean tree reproduced the voided run's one-year result to four decimals, so the edits had not touched a forecast

impact.provenance: the runner's own record and the re-run

notes: The runner refuses a worktree with uncommitted changes and records whether it stayed clean through the run.
The scorer refuses any arm whose code differs from the commit its run names, which also covers runs made before that record existed.

changes.title: Three ways the scorer could have misread a review
changes.what_changed: A substring search would have voided a clean arm whose reviewer wrote 'no leak found'. A regex emptied every section. And the first real review titled itself with the arm's name, which the parser took as the arm's section and read as unreadable.

recorded.headline: no verdict was ever wrong
recorded.detail: each failure was safe: an unreadable review is never counted as clean

impact.provenance: fixtures, including the real review that exposed the third

notes: Verdicts are computed by code from each arm's own files, so a misparse would have moved a verdict silently.

changes.title: The runner asked only for the 90% interval
changes.what_changed: The comparison was run at one confidence level, so the family-wise interval the decision rule needs did not exist.

recorded.headline: no arm could have reached CONFIRMED
recorded.detail: and each report would have recorded that absence as a result

impact.provenance: found before any arm was scored

changes.status: fixed: both levels come from one set of resamples

changes.what_changed: A committed canonical output, a three-band comparison (identical, numerical within 1e-9, moved), categorical changes listed first, and a paired per-forecast comparison with moving-block bootstrap intervals at two confidence levels from one set of resamples.

recorded.headline: every claim of 'nothing changed' in this work is a measured 0 of 387

changes.what_changed: Perturb every observation unavailable at a cutoff date, including inside each series' publication lag, and require every forecast issued up to that date to come out byte-identical.

recorded.headline: caught a real leak in main the first time it ran
recorded.detail: and it has been seen to fail on purpose since

impact.provenance: ADR 0009 and each arm's audit record

changes.status: in use; two known blind spots recorded as D14 and D15

changes.title: One worktree per idea, and an assertion that it imports its own code
changes.what_changed: Each arm runs in its own git worktree with a private cache copy. The package is an editable install pointing at main, so without an explicit assertion every branch would silently have reported main's results as its own.

recorded.headline: the control arm proves it works
recorded.detail: A0 reproduces main exactly, and every other arm's outputs carry its own configuration hash

changes.title: Pre-registration, and verdicts computed by code
changes.what_changed: Each experiment's decision rule, confidence levels and family-wise correction are committed before anything runs; verdicts are computed from each arm's own output files rather than read off a report. Experiments 0003, 0004 and 0005 each had their reading rule committed before their data existed.

recorded.headline: three results the rule made unarguable
recorded.detail: A4 confirmed, the seed check robust, and the state-count ablation inconclusive because main's own gate rejects sixteen unrestricted regimes

limits: Every idea was designed by someone who had already seen main's results, so confirmed in sample is the ceiling this design can reach. Out-of-sample confirmation comes only from forecasts registered forward, the first resolving 2027-07-01.

Pricing that forward test: about 9.5 months to the first data point, which is ten correlated same-date resolutions rather than one independent observation; roughly three years for a directional read; roughly 31 years to match the backtest's 31.5 independent one-year windows.

A4's gain is confounded. The structure and the regime count changed together, and its one-year gain landed on the at-horizon questions (+0.0884) rather than the any-time ones (+0.0297), the opposite of its own hypothesis. The ablation that would separate them reads inconclusive: main's gate rejects sixteen unrestricted regimes as too short-lived and too small.

A4 assumes growth is uncorrelated with inflation and rates within each joint regime, and that is false in the data. Measured on the fitting panel, the discarded dependence runs at roughly half to two thirds of the dependence the model does keep: three independent computations — the committed derivation (research/briefings/derivations/within_state_cross_block_correlation.py), an independent reviewer's, and a run against the cached four-by-four fits — put the ratio between 0.51 and 0.67. The exact digits move with which fitted model and which day's panel is measured, so the size is the finding and the third decimal is not.
Each A4 forecast rests on thinner evidence: about 45 to 48 months of effective sample per regime, against 112 to 122 for main.
Ten-year evidence is about 2.2 independent observations. No ten-year number here is informative.
The one-year calibration gate cannot be passed reliably at this sample size: a perfectly calibrated forecaster fails it about 91% of the time at n = 31.

decisions.title: Register A4's forecasts forward
decisions.detail: Beside the shipped configuration's, so both are scored as they resolve from 2027-07-01. It is the only out-of-sample test there is, and it is outward-facing.

decisions.title: The Anvil adjudication
decisions.detail: The stress-test dossier leaves decision and classification blank by design: your decision in your words, and one of FACTUAL, MECHANICAL, TASTE or SCOPE.

decisions.title: The calibration gate at n = 31
decisions.detail: Keep it and report the one-year failure as uninformative, or register a new sample-size-aware test. Moving the threshold is not an option.

decisions.title: Re-shipping
decisions.detail: The committed submission still carries the benchmark's pre-fix base rates, which moved by at most 0.0061.

decisions.title: A materiality floor for judged leaks
decisions.detail: A6 is void for a leak that moves its one-year difference by 0.0002, because the rule voids for any path. Whether a future registration should state a size below which a found leak is recorded but does not void an arm is a choice for next time.

decisions.title: The layer table, or the imports (D16)
decisions.detail: Seven imports disagree with the package's declared layer order, all pre-dating this session. Either the imports move -- real surgery in data and features -- or the table is rewritten to describe the package as it is. layer_check exits 0 either way today, so nothing forces the question.

next_candidates.title: Couple the two chains
next_candidates.detail: The top-ranked extension in briefing 04, and the only one that makes the model more than two separate chains. Diagonal coupling costs four parameters, the forward pass already pays the computational cost, and the measured block-independence violation above is the evidence for it. It carries a free falsifier: the joint second eigenvalue equals the slower chain's only while the chains are independent.
next_candidates.provability: UNDERPOWERED, and aimed at the wrong quantity. Briefing 05 derives the detectable one-year difference as 0.018 at 90% and 0.026 at 98.33%, against a plausible effect near 0.005. It also finds a quantity mismatch: the dependence A4 discards is contemporaneous, in the emission covariance, while coupling changes transitions and leaves that covariance block-diagonal.

next_candidates.title: Time-varying transitions on the growth chain
next_candidates.detail: The factorial structure cuts the parameter cost about twentyfold against putting them on a joint chain, which converts an objection the earlier briefing treated as fatal into a survivable one.
next_candidates.provability: UNDERPOWERED. The parameter-cost claim is proven (12q against 240q, a twentyfold saving), but the forecasting claim needs an effect near 0.005 against a floor of 0.018 to 0.030 — and the proposed driver's own measured skill in this window is negative.

next_candidates.title: A state-count ablation main's gate will accept
next_candidates.detail: The K = 16 ablation could not be fitted. Separating structure from granularity needs a new pre-registration at a count the regimes-exist gate admits.
next_candidates.provability: NOT FALSIFIABLE AS STATED, and provable once rewritten: two chains at 2x3, six joint cells matching main's six exactly, holding granularity fixed and varying only structure. Its two hypotheses predict outcomes about 0.06 apart against a floor near 0.025, and it resolves the confound ADR 0010 admits. Register this one first.

how_to_update: Append an entry to research/reports/impact-analysis/changes.json and rebuild. An entry whose impact is {"from_arm": "<arm>"} has its numbers resolved live from that arm's own paired.json through score_slate.py, so the page cannot disagree with the files. An entry whose impact is {"recorded": {...}, "provenance": "..."} states where the number came from. Then run .venv/bin/python research/tools/build_impact_analysis.py and republish to the same URL.
